messages.subject_clean: Error in make.capthist for Transect Data
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I've been trying to import transect scat survey data into secr for analysis. Unfortunately I've run into an issue I can't seem to rectify on my own.

The problem is with how secr is interpreting my trap data. I've formatted the data as described in the datainput.pdf for polygons, which is supposed to work with transect data as well. Below is a sample of the original data I've imported into R from a .csv file (called "transects"), then what the data looks like once I've used the read.traps function to format the data appropriately to move forward (called "transects1"). The problem is the function doesn't seem to be recognizing my "detectorID" column, and is instead saying I have 126 separate transects instead of 4. The x and y coordinates are in UTMs (zone 35N), if that helps with any troubleshooting. I must be formatting my data incorrectly somewhere along the line to cause this error, but I've attempted this several times over from step 1, including skipping the read.traps function and using make.capthist function, but it interprets the trap data the same way (126 transects instead of 4). I've also tried  importing directly from .txt files using read.capthist, but it seems to encounter the same error and I get the message that "argument lengths differ". I'm happy to provide more information if needed. Any insight or guidance is much appreciated. Thanks!

messages.body_plain:
Try changing the name of your detectorID field to transectID [names(transects)[1] <- "transectID"]. It also works (without any name issues) if you read directly from a text file with the transectID in the first column.

Not sure where this is documented, if at all, but you might have got a clue from looking at the code - just type read.traps at the R prompt - and scanning for 'transect', as I did!
Murray

messages.subject: animal identifier across multiple sessions
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I am new to this forum and new to SECR so please forgive me if my question is uninformed.

I would like to use the R package ‘secr’ to generate density estimates for feral cats using camera traps. My cameras traps (n = 72) have been operating for 25 days each month since October 2015. I would like to generate separate density estimates for each month.

My question is: does the animal identifier used in ‘secr’ relate to one session (i.e. month) only, or does it apply across multiple sessions? To put it another way, some individual cats appear on the camera traps across several months (sessions). So if “Animal 2” from the October session also appears on the camera traps in the December session, is that animal still called “Animal 2” in the December session or do I ‘wipe the slate clean’ each session and forget about individual animals identified previously?

Hopefully that makes sense.

Thanks in advance for your time.

Regards,

               Andrew

messages.subject: Re: animal identifier across multiple sessions
messages.body_plain:
Hi Andrew
Welcome to the group.

Strictly, when 'secr.fit' fits a multi-session model, the slate is wiped clean each session. However, this should not stop you from using animal identifiers consistently from one session to the next. This makes data checking much easier, and ultimately you may want to use the same dataset for an open population analysis (spatial or non-spatial) for which it is necessary to build capture histories across sessions. The only route to open population analysis at present is to export data to RMark (see first example in ?RMarkInput). That is of course non-spatial. I have some other code for open SECR that will not be public for at least 6 months.

"wiping the slate clean" is cheating to some extent: the confidence intervals are calculated on the assumption that each session (realisation) is independent. Sampling of animals that survive in the same home ranges violates this; the solution is to determine CI laboriously by parametric bootstrapping (sampling from simulated data). I haven't seen anyone actually do this!
Murray

Murray

messages.subject: Multisession model
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,
I fitted a multi-session model with six sessions and related habitat masks:

m2 <- secr.fit(capthist = 'leo', model=list(D~1, g0~1, sigma~scale(dRes)), buffer=30000, mask=leoudzmask, ncores = 25)

and I got this error:
Fitted (real) parameters evaluated at base levels of covariates
Error in lpred[, 1] <- mat %*% beta[indx] : replacement has length zero.

Please find attached a reproducible example that can be loaded with the following command:

library(session)
restore.session("trial1.RSession")

In the R session you can also find the "m2" object.

Best,
Rasmus

messages.subject: Re: Multisession model
messages.body_plain:
Hi Rasmus
What were you meaning with 'scale(dRes)'? The model specification code in 'secr' does not allow you to transform predictors on the fly like this. Use covariates()$scaled.dRes <- scale(covariates()$dRes) then ... sigma ~ scaled.dRes...

Some other points -

These data look promising!

I couldn't re-run all your code because it requires raw data files that were not included (I'm not asking for these!)

You don't need to attach the 'parallel' library to use multiple cores - the parallel functions are accessed internally. Also, using multiple cores usually takes _longer_ with secr.fit, and at most one core should be specified per session.

Your buffer width 30 km seems way larger than the data require. I'd suggest around 6 km on the basis of 4 x RPSV(leo, CC=T).

Trap covariate names can be specified within read.traps (the covnames argument) rather than requiring an extra statement.

I also question the wisdom of modelling varying sigma without allowing for reciprocal variation in g0 or lambda0.

Murray

messages.subject: Capture hisotry covariates in ClosedN
messages.body_plain:
Hi All,

I am trying to use the function closedN() to estimate population size from harvest data (i.e. where recapture probability = 0 because a capture is typically a hunted animal).

Is it possible to analyze models in closedN with covariates associated with the capture history? I tried adding covariate data using the function covariate(), however, the model outcome does not appear to change when covariates are included.

Many thanks,
Steve

messages.subject: Re: Capture hisotry covariates in ClosedN
messages.body_plain:
No. closedN() merely provides some old-fashioned estimators, about at the level of the CAPTURE package. 'secr' is not trying to compete with MARK!
Murray
